bible.title: Swan Lock
bible.premise: A canal lock with a pub beside it, where salt barges tied up for a night and waited for the water.
bible.collapse: On 10 October, after the darts final at the Swan, lock-keeper Kofi Brandt bet landlady Marit Oyelaran 3 pints he could fill the lock in under 9 minutes, opened all 4 paddles on the top gate and went to bed. The pound drained overnight and 17 barges sat down in the mud with their crews aboard.

people.name: Kofi Brandt
people.want: to win one bet off Marit Oyelaran

people.name: Marit Oyelaran
people.want: the slate paid off before winter

people.name: Nell Brandt
people.want: her mum home by her birthday

people.name: Dagny Roos
people.want: to be through the lock before the frost

events.fact: Oyelaran chalked Brandt's tab on the slate at 41 pints and stopped his credit.
Brandt bet Oyelaran 3 pints he could fill the lock in under 9 minutes.
Brandt opened all 4 paddles on the top gate with his brass windlass and went to bed.
The pound was dry for 2 miles. 17 barges sat in the mud, the Patience nearest the gate.
Roos shared the Patience's 30 tins of peaches between 17 crews.
Eels came out of the mud into the Swan's cellar. Oyelaran counted 60 and shut the cellar hatch.
Brandt dropped the brass windlass into the lock chamber and went down the ladder after it.

authors.name: Nell Brandt
authors.document: letters to her mum in a school exercise book
authors.register: Opens Dear Mum. Counts sleeps to her birthday. Long sentences joined with and. Repeats what grown-ups said word for word.
authors.never: thinks her dad did anything wrong

authors.name: Marit Oyelaran
authors.document: the slate behind the bar: tabs, bets and who is barred
authors.register: A name, then what is owed in pints. Settles an argument in one line. No dates unless somebody is barred.
authors.never: writes down a bet without the stake

authors.name: Dagny Roos
authors.document: verses made up at the tiller and painted on the Patience's cabin
authors.register: Four short lines, second and fourth rhymed. Counts barges, miles and tins. Rude about lock-keepers.
authors.never: puts her own name in a verse

enemies.husk: barge crews sunk to the waist in the pound
enemies.swarmling: eels out of the drained pound
enemies.spewer: bilge pumps left running on the barges
enemies.guardian: Kofi Brandt at the top gate with the brass windlass

exemplars.author: Nell Brandt
exemplars.title: Letter to Mum, 12 sleeps
exemplars.source: pencil, page 9 of a school exercise book
exemplars.text: Dear Mum, it is 12 sleeps to my birthday. Dad had a bet with Mrs Oyelaran at the darts that he can fill the lock in under 9 minutes, and she said he could not fill a kettle in 9 minutes, and everybody laughed. It is for 3 pints. He took the brass windlass out after closing and told me to go to bed and I did, but I heard all 4 paddles go up because they squeak. He came in whistling. Please write back and say which day. Love, Nell.

exemplars.author: Marit Oyelaran
exemplars.title: The slate, left column
exemplars.source: chalk on the slate behind the Swan's bar
exemplars.text: K. BRANDT: 41 pints. Nothing more on the slate till 20 are paid. He says the company pays him Friday. It has been Friday twice.

exemplars.author: Marit Oyelaran
exemplars.title: The slate, bets
exemplars.source: chalk, boxed off in the corner of the slate
exemplars.text: BET. Brandt says he fills the lock in under 9 minutes. I say he doesn't. Stake 3 pints. Witnessed by the Swan darts team, who are no use as witnesses after ten o'clock.

exemplars.author: Dagny Roos
exemplars.title: Verse, port side
exemplars.source: white paint on the cabin side of the Patience
exemplars.text: 17 barges went to bed afloat / and woke up sat in clay. / 2 miles of pound went down the lock / for 3 pints at the Swan, they say.

exemplars.author: Nell Brandt
exemplars.title: Letter to Mum, 3 sleeps
exemplars.source: a page torn from an exercise book, folded small
exemplars.text: Dear Mum, 3 sleeps. There are eels in the cellar of the Swan. Mrs Oyelaran counted 60 and then shut the cellar hatch and said a word. Dad says eels can walk over land if the grass is wet, which I did not believe, and now I have seen it. I am putting this one under the door of the Patience because Mrs Roos says she will post it when she floats.

exemplars.author: Marit Oyelaran
exemplars.title: The slate, barred list
exemplars.source: chalk, gone over twice so it will not rub off
exemplars.text: BARRED: K. Brandt, for life or until he refills the pound, whichever comes first. Went down the lock chamber ladder on the 25th after that brass windlass. 44 pints. I am leaving it up.

exemplars.author: Marit Oyelaran
exemplars.title: R. Asante's tin mug
exemplars.source: a dented tin mug on a belt hook
exemplars.text: A tin mug with R. Asante scratched on the base and mud from the pound dried to the rim. He had 2 pints on the slate from the darts final. Oyelaran rubbed them off herself, which she has done for nobody else.

exemplars.author: Nell Brandt
exemplars.title: Eel number 61
exemplars.source: an eel, a beer mat stuck to its side
exemplars.text: An eel as long as Nell's arm, which she measured. There is a Swan beer mat stuck to it. Mrs Oyelaran stopped counting at 60, so this is 61.

exemplars.author: Dagny Roos
exemplars.title: B. Imre's pump handle
exemplars.source: an iron bilge pump handle, grip worn pale
exemplars.text: Pump handle off the Patience, worn pale where two hands go. B. Imre pumped from 11 October until there was nothing under the hull to pump. Roos gave him a line on the cabin: pumped all night and raised the mud an inch.

exemplars.author: Marit Oyelaran
exemplars.title: Brandt's brass windlass
exemplars.source: a brass windlass with a bootlace through the handle
exemplars.text: Brass windlass, the square socket worn nearly round. On 10 October it opened all 4 paddles on the top gate. Found at the foot of the lock chamber ladder. Oyelaran took it against the tab: 1 pint off, 43 to go.
Two barges lean together in the mud. Crew stand waist deep between the hulls, facing the door.
The Swan's cellar. A barrel sits on the hatch and the barrel is rocking.
All 4 paddles are up. Water crosses the floor knee high; the gate walkway above it is dry.

exemplars.author: Nell Brandt
exemplars.name: Nell's Exercise Book
exemplars.text: Nell Brandt wrote her mum 14 letters in it and posted none. The back page is her map of where the mud will hold a person.

exemplars.author: Dagny Roos
exemplars.name: Roos's Tin Opener
exemplars.text: Dagny Roos shared 30 tins between 17 crews and kept the opener. People were very polite to her after that.

exemplars.author: Marit Oyelaran
exemplars.name: Red Flights
exemplars.text: Marit Oyelaran throws three darts with red flights. She has not bought her own drink at a Swan final in 6 years.

exemplars.author: Dagny Roos
exemplars.name: Tinned Peaches
exemplars.text: Restores 20 Integrity. One of 30 tins off the Patience. The label says serves four, which Roos read as a suggestion.

exemplars.author: Marit Oyelaran
exemplars.name: Swan Beer Mat
exemplars.text: Blocks the next hit. The Swan had 500 printed. Most of them are under table legs.

exemplars.author: Marit Oyelaran
exemplars.name: Pint on the Slate
exemplars.text: Doubles damage for 5 s. Oyelaran chalks it up against whoever is standing nearest the bar.

exemplars.name: The Pound
exemplars.text: Two miles of canal with the water let out. 17 barges, all leaning.

exemplars.name: The Swan
exemplars.text: The darts final is still chalked up. There is a barrel on the cellar hatch.

exemplars.name: Top Gate
exemplars.text: 4 paddles up since 10 October, and the only windlass is down the chamber.
BRANDT SWINGS THE WINDLASS WIDE. STAY INSIDE HIS ARM.
PADDLES UP. THE CHAMBER'S FILLING. CLIMB.
SIXTY EELS OUT OF THE CELLAR HATCH. BACKS TO THE BAR.
UNDER 9 MINUTES, HE SAID. COUNT HIM DOWN FROM THE WALKWAY.
